_comment: Light WS2 (light-2) - no printed key; answers DERIVED from physics with sign convention.

_excluded_figures.desc: Optical instruments hidden inside boxes (a) and (b); options describe ray-convergence behaviour shown in the diagrams - needs the figure.
Parallel rays from a distant tree on a convex lens; the four options are themselves ray diagrams (a/b/c/d images) - figure-dependent.
Object LMNO placed beyond C of a concave mirror as shown in figure; asks shape of the image - needs the figure geometry.
Two plane mirrors A and B at angle A (given only in the figure); number of reflections before the ray emerges - needs angle A from the figure.
Square room PQRS (8 m) with a full-length plane mirror on PQ, camera at point M, point R - positions of M and R are only in the figure.
Rectangular glass block PQRS, critical angle 39 degree, pin midway on face PQ; where it appears from face PS - needs ray-trace through the figure.
Converging set of rays from water (n=4/3) onto a plane interface, geometry of convergence point shown in the figure - figure-dependent.

2.reason: Plane-mirror image is virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted -> 'virtual'.

4.reason: Convex mirror: f is positive; object at infinity gives a virtual image behind the mirror so image distance v is also positive -> (+, +).

5.reason: Increasing angle of incidence increases the angle of refraction (Snell's law).

6.reason: A bundle/group of light rays is called a beam of light.

7.reason: A distant object (distant tree) gives nearly parallel rays so the image forms at the focus; the distant tree is the standard object.

8.reason: For a distant object the real image forms at the focus, so f = distance between the mirror and the screen.

10.reason: Concave mirror gives a magnified real image when the object is between F and C (image then forms beyond C).

11.reason: Object beyond 2F (>2f): real, inverted, diminished image formed between F and 2F (Between F and 2F).

12.reason: Maximum bending/refraction occurs in the medium of highest refractive index; 1.71 = material C.

14.reason: The mirror placed near the wall opposite the window catches the real image of the distant window on that wall.

15.reason: Minimum angle of refraction = maximum bending = highest n = 1.65 = medium C.

17.reason: For a distant object the image forms at the focus, so f = distance between the lens and the screen.

18.reason: Each part of the lens forms the full image so a complete image is produced (S1 true); covering half only reduces brightness (S2 true), but reduced intensity does not explain why the image is complete -> not the correct explanation.

20.reason: A point source at the focus of a concave mirror (or a convex lens) produces a parallel beam after reflection/refraction.

21.reason: To get a real image on a screen, the candle is placed beyond the focus of the concave mirror.

22.reason: REVIEW: For an object at infinity each device forms a point-sized diminished image at its focus (concave mirror real point; convex mirror, concave & convex lens also point images), so the all-four option is the best fit; option wording is ambiguous.

26.reason: Same-size real image from a convex lens forms when the object is at 2f (twice the focal length).

28.reason: Refractive index is least for the longest wavelength (least deviation) -> red light.

29.reason: Parallel rays from a distant object converge at the focus (f) of a convex lens.

30.reason: A convex mirror diverges reflected rays -> diverging mirror.

31.reason: Lateral shift through a parallel slab is directly proportional to the slab thickness.

33.reason: An always-erect image at any distance is given by a plane OR a convex mirror -> either plane or convex.

34.reason: In pin experiments the pins are placed so that their feet appear collinear (in a straight line).

35.reason: A plane surface has infinite focal length, so power P = 1/f = 0 (zero).

36.reason: Maximum refraction/bending occurs in the highest-n medium; 2.42 = substance R.

37.reason: With a lamp and a screen the image of the lamp at the focus gives the focal length (lamp acts as the source, screen catches the image).

38.reason: Parallel rays (parallel to the principal axis) converge at the principal focus on the axis.

39.reason: REVIEW: All distant-object sources (window, sun, distant tree) can find a lens's focal length; option (a) with an object at 10 cm (< f = 30 cm) cannot. Single intended answer is ambiguous among b/c/d; chose the lab 'light from window'.

40.reason: Cutting a lens into two halves without changing the curvature does not change the focal length; each half still has focal length f.

41.reason: As the object moves from 2f to f, the real image moves from 2f to infinity, so it travels an infinite distance.

42.reason: A ray along the principal axis hits the pole and emerges/retraces along the principal axis; 'emerge out along the principal axis'.

43.reason: REVIEW: A plane mirror always gives a virtual, erect, same-size image regardless of object position; among the listed options the 'convex mirror' choice (image nature unchanged - always virtual, erect, diminished) is selected as the best fit since no plane-mirror option is given.

44.reason: Slide projector: slide is between f and 2f of the converging lens, giving a real, magnified, inverted image on the screen.

45.reason: Law of reflection: angle of reflection always equals angle of incidence.

46.reason: Optical fibres work on total internal reflection.

47.reason: Real, same-size image from a convex lens forms when the object is at 2F.

48.reason: Concave mirror gives a real, inverted, same-size image when the object is at the centre of curvature.

49.reason: Light incident along the normal is not refracted (passes straight, only changes speed).

51.reason: Correct order: select object (3=C) -> hold lens parallel to screen (4=D) -> adjust for sharp image (2=B) -> measure distance (1=A) => C, D, B, A.

52.reason: Real images are always inverted and virtual images are always erect; both statements are correct.

53.reason: Dentists use CONCAVE mirrors (not convex) for a magnified image of teeth, so statement 1 is incorrect -> (A).

54.reason: Convex lens with +4 D gives f = 1/4 = +0.25 m (true). The other options have the wrong power sign or wrong magnitude.

55.reason: A real image forms where rays actually meet/converge: statements 1 and 2 -> (A) and (B).

56.reason: Rarer->denser bends TOWARD the normal and denser->rarer bends AWAY; so statements 1 and 4 are incorrect -> A and D.

57.reason: All four statements are correct (speed same in vacuum, differs in denser media, c=3e8 m/s in air, n is dimensionless) -> All of these.

58.reason: Virtual images cannot be projected, are formed by both concave and convex lenses, and are always erect (never inverted) -> (A),(B),(C).

59.reason: A make-up (concave) mirror gives a magnified erect image -> object within focal length (u<f). Only Case II (u=10 < f=15) satisfies this -> Case II.

60.reason: Correct slab result needs r<i and i=e (emergent parallel to incident). Student I (i=60, r=35, e=59) has r<i and i approx e -> I.

61.reason: For a parallel slab the emergent angle equals the incident angle; Student C has i=30 and e=30 (equal) with r=17<30 -> C.

62.reason: When object distance = image distance the object is at 2f: here 30 cm = 30 cm, so 2f = 30 => f = 15 cm.

63.reason: REVIEW: Among the options the largest pin separation gives the most accurate result; student 4 (15 cm) wins over the identical-angle student 3 (10 cm) -> D. (The printed angle values are physically inconsistent.)

64.reason: Through a parallel slab the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray -> statement 3 = (C).

65.reason: A more distant object (tree) forms its image closer to the lens (near the focus), so the lens must be moved towards the screen.

66.reason: For a distant lamp the image forms closer to the lens, so reduce the lens-screen gap: move the screen towards the lens OR the lens towards the screen.

67.reason: REVIEW: For a plane mirror, an observer approaching a stationary object sees the image approach at twice the observer's speed: 2 x 2 = 4 m/s.

68.reason: REVIEW: Statement 1 is wrong (use one outline, not three positions) and statement 4 is wrong (fixing pins from the other side locates the EMERGENT ray, not the refracted ray) -> guidelines 4 and 1 = D and A.

69.reason: The sun (infinity) forms its image at the focus, slightly closer than the far candle's image, so the lens is moved slightly towards the screen.

70.reason: Head bigger = concave (object within f), middle same size = plane, legs smaller = convex; from top: Concave, plane and convex.

71.reason: A more distant object (tree) forms its image closer to the lens (towards the focus), so the lens is moved towards the screen.

72.reason: REVIEW: To catch the real image of a distant object you need a screen, a mirror holder and a scale to measure the distance = setup 1 = (A). Setups without a screen cannot show the image.

73.reason: Best setup uses moderate angles (30,45,60 avoid large errors at extreme angles) and the larger 8 cm pin separation for accuracy = option 3 = (C).

74.reason: A distant object forms a real, inverted image at the focus for both: convex lens d1=20 cm (inverted) and concave mirror d2=20 cm (inverted) -> (20 cm, 20 cm) and (inverted, inverted).

75.reason: The concave mirror placed near the wall opposite the window forms the real image of the distant window on that opposite wall.
